The person behind the drawings

I drew my first house at a kitchen table in Roztoky — my parents’ house, designed at night after shifts at a big Prague practice that built shopping centres. It leaked once, in the first winter, at a detail I had drawn too confidently. My father fixed it with me. I have drawn carefully ever since.

Nineteen years and forty-seven houses later, the method has not changed: I draw by hand first, because a pencil makes you decide; then a cardboard model, because a client should hold the house before they pay for it; only then the computer, for the documents the building office needs.

I take two, at most three houses at a time, and I am on site every week while they are built. Most of my plots are difficult — steep, narrow, protected, overlooked. A difficult plot is not a problem to hide. It is usually the reason the house ends up interesting.

  1. 2007
    A house for his parents

    First built work: a timber house in Roztoky, drawn at night while employed by a large Prague practice. It is still standing, and still teaching him.

  2. 2011
    The atelier

    Tomas leaves the big practice and opens a one-man atelier in Vinohrady. First rule on the wall: two houses at a time, never four.

  3. 2017
    The protected street

    First reconstruction inside a heritage zone — four months of argument with the conservation office, and a façade that kept every one of its 1908 openings.

  4. 2026
    Forty-seven houses

    The forty-seventh house is finished in Troja. The atelier is still one man, one drawing table, and a shelf of white models.

Before you ask

Do you take projects outside Prague?

Yes — Central Bohemia is home ground, and weekly site visits are included in the fee within about 60 km. Further away, visits are planned in blocks around the building milestones, and the study stage is done from Prague with two long site days.

How long does a house take, start to finish?

Honestly: the study takes two to three months, the permit documentation three to four. The permit itself runs on the building office’s calendar — in Prague, count on six to twelve months. Building takes twelve to eighteen. If someone promises you a house in a year, they are selling, not drawing.

Our plot is in a heritage zone. What changes?

The conservation office must state its position before the building permit, and it argues about façades, roofs and window openings — in that order. Tomas prepares the heritage dossier himself and goes to the meetings in person. Two of the six houses above went through it; both kept their original openings.

Can you work with our own builder?

Yes, and often. One condition: author supervision stays with Tomas at five fixed milestones — foundations, shell, roof, services, finishes — whoever holds the contract. That is how details drawn carefully stay built carefully.

How are the fees paid?

In the three stages the calculator shows: the study on its delivery, the documentation when the permit application goes in, supervision monthly while the house is built. No percentage of the building cost, no surprise lines — the estimate on this page is the fee structure, not a teaser.
